name: Tadasana
description: The foundation of every standing pose — trains even weight, a long spine, and calm focus.
instructions: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart, weight spread evenly across both feet.
Engage your thighs and lift your kneecaps slightly, without locking your knees.
Lengthen your spine and reach the crown of your head toward the ceiling.
Relax your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Let your arms rest naturally by your sides, palms facing forward.

name: Vrikshasana
description: Tests balance, leg strength, and hip alignment by standing tall on one leg.
instructions: Start standing tall in Tadasana, then shift your weight onto one leg.
Bend your other knee and place the sole of that foot on your inner calf or inner thigh — never on the knee.
Press your foot and standing leg together to find balance.
Keep your hips level and facing forward.
Bring your hands to your heart, or raise them overhead once you feel steady.

name: Trikonasana
description: A wide standing stretch that opens the hips, hamstrings, and side body.
instructions: Step your feet wide apart, about one leg's length.
Turn your front foot to point forward, and angle your back foot slightly inward.
Extend both arms out to shoulder height.
Hinge at your front hip and reach your front hand toward your shin, ankle, or the floor.
Stretch your other arm straight up, stacking your shoulders and keeping your chest open.

name: Virabhadrasana I
description: A grounded lunge with arms overhead — builds leg strength and an open chest.
instructions: Step one foot back into a wide, deep lunge.
Bend your front knee to about a right angle, keeping it stacked above your ankle.
Straighten your back leg and press your back heel toward the floor.
Square your hips and chest toward the front of your mat.
Raise both arms straight overhead, reaching up alongside your ears.

name: Utkatasana
description: An imaginary chair sit that builds heat and strength through the legs and core.
instructions: Stand with your feet together or hip-width apart.
Bend your knees and sit your hips back, as if lowering into an invisible chair.
Keep your knees behind your toes and your weight in your heels.
Lengthen your spine forward slightly, without rounding your back.
Raise both arms overhead, reaching up alongside your ears.

name: Virabhadrasana II
description: A wide, powerful stance with arms extended — builds stamina and hip opening.
instructions: Step your feet wide apart into a strong stance.
Turn your front foot forward and bend that knee to about a right angle.
Keep your back leg straight and strong.
Extend both arms out to shoulder height, front arm reaching over your front leg.
Turn your head to gaze out over your front hand.
